editorial:
Imagine leaving your comfortable life in Britain to help people in the Dominican Republic, only to vanish without a trace. That is the scary setup you get here. You follow a young woman who thinks she is doing a good deed, but she quickly finds herself in way over her head. The real heart of the story, though, is her parents. You feel their panic and sadness as they travel to a foreign land to find out what happened to their daughter. It feels like a mix of a mystery and a family drama that keeps you wondering if she is actually safe or gone for good.

The acting is really solid and makes the emotional parts feel real. While the pacing starts a bit slow, the tension builds up nicely as the parents uncover dark secrets. It is not a loud action movie, but it keeps you on edge. If you enjoy stories about family loyalty and solving a puzzle, you should definitely check this out. Since it is an older TV movie, you might have to hunt for it on digital rental stores like Apple TV, but it is worth adding the physical disc to your collection if you find a remastered version for a better picture.
endingExplained: You find out that the daughter was caught up in local corruption and political greed. The parents eventually discover that she was held against her will because she saw things she wasn't supposed to see. In the final scenes, the truth comes out about who betrayed her. While the ending provides some closure and answers for the family, it leaves you feeling a bit sad about how easily a good person can be hurt by powerful people.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves family mysteries and political thrillers.
